newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU opens probe into loans to former Vulkan yards.
newsitem.headline: EU opens probe into loans to former Vulkan yards.

text.p: The European Commission said on Tuesday it had started a probe into some 300 million marks in loans granted to Bremer Vulkan's former shipyards in east Germany, MTW-Schiffswerft and Volkswerft Stralsund.

It said in a statement that the probe did not prejudge of its current examination of an overall aid package for the yards, which have been deprived of 788 million marks in public subsidies by their parent company.

The Commission's decision on Tuesday was due to the fact that the loans paid by the German privatisation agency BvS and the authorities of the state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern -- which now own the yards -- had not received its green light.

The Commission said it could not accept "the German argument that the loans did not have to be notified in advance as they are a replacement for authorised aid" which was syphoned by Vulkan prior to its collapse earlier this year.
It suggested that the loans themselves amounted to subsidies saying it was doubtful that private banks would have lent the money given the "highly critical economic situation" of the yards.

The German authorities have requested the Commission's permission for a new aid package worth almost one billion marks to rescue MTW-Schiffswerft and Volkswerft, European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert told reporters last month.
Van Miert has pledged some understanding for the problems encountered by the two yards as a result of the misuse by Vulkan of German subsidies intended for them.

But he warned that EU industry ministers would be asked to give their assent on the new package. The payment of huge subsidies to the German shipbuilding industry has faced with the strong opposition of the Danish shipyards backed by their government.
